title: Microsoft Purview: audit logs for role and scoped-role permission checks (GCC, GCC High and DoD)
summary: The briefing matches the government-cloud roadmap record and accurately documents the existing audit controls. Minor corrections should clarify the product-level licensing, extend the role-group navigation to its membership control, and cite the documentation connecting that PowerShell command to Purview roles.

Replace the notes with: 'The existing Audit (Standard) or Audit (Premium) organisation subscription and per-user licensing requirements apply. Keep https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-get-started as the source; do not assert that the new events are Premium-only.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Audit > Search reaches the tenant's general audit search page.
claims.quote: Select the Audit solution card. If the Audit solution card isn't displayed, select View all solutions and then select Audit from the Core section. On the Search page, configure the following search criteria as applicable:

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog -StartDate <start> -EndDate <end> -Operations <operation names> searches the unified audit log by date and operation.
claims.quote: Search-UnifiedAuditLog -StartDate 5/1/2023 -EndDate 5/8/2023 -RecordType SharePointFileOperation -Operations FileAccessed -SessionId "WordDocs_SharepointViews" -SessionCommand ReturnLargeSet

claims.claim: Exact operation names are entered in Activities - operations names.
claims.quote: Activities - operations names: Enter the exact operation names to search for audited activities to include in your search results.

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog runs in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: The underlying cmdlet used to search the audit log is an Exchange Online cmdlet, which is Search-UnifiedAuditLog. ... You have to run this cmdlet in Exchange Online PowerShell.

claims.claim: Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups reaches the Purview role groups used to manage audit access.
claims.quote: Go to Settings > Roles and scopes ... Select Role groups. ... select a Microsoft Purview role group you want to add users to. Select Edit on the control bar. ... select Choose users or Choose groups.
claims.fix: Extend controls[1].ui.path and the rendered table path to 'Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > role group > Edit > Choose users' for adding individual users, as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/purview-permissions#add-users-or-groups-to-a-microsoft-purview-built-in-role-group. The current path stops early on the correct listing page.

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity <role group> -Member <user> grants a user the roles assigned to a Purview role group.
claims.quote: Add-RoleGroupMember [-Identity] <RoleGroupIdParameter> -Member <SecurityPrincipalIdParameter> ... When you add a member to a role group, the member is given the effective permissions provided by the management roles assigned to the role group.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/m365-workload-docs#microsoft-365 to sources. Its management API reference explicitly documents Add-RoleGroupMember for Purview-specific roles in Security & Compliance PowerShell; the cited command reference supplies the syntax.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Audit Reader and Audit Manager have the audit-search roles assigned by default.
claims.quote: Admins and members of investigation teams must be assigned the View-Only Audit Logs or Audit Logs role ... By default, the Microsoft Purview portal Role groups page assigns these roles to the Audit Reader and Audit Manager role groups.

claims.claim: Viewing Purview role groups requires Global Administrator or the Role Management role.
claims.quote: To view Role groups in the Roles and scopes area in the Microsoft Purview portal, users need to be a global administrator or need to be assigned the Role Management role

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Audit > Start recording user and admin activity turns on general tenant auditing.
claims.quote: Select the Audit solution card. ... If auditing isn't turned on for your organization, a banner is displayed prompting you to start recording user and admin activity. Select the Start recording user and admin activity banner.

claims.claim: Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true turns on general tenant auditing in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: Connect to Exchange Online PowerShell. Run the following PowerShell command to turn on auditing. Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true

claims.claim: The start-recording banner is displayed when tenant auditing is off.
claims.quote: If auditing isn't turned on for your organization, a banner is displayed prompting you to start recording user and admin activity.

claims.claim: Turning auditing on or off requires the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online to turn auditing on or off.

claims.claim: Learn describes audit logging as on by default for Microsoft 365 organisations in the enterprise context of this briefing.
claims.quote: Audit log search is turned on by default for Microsoft 365 and Office 365 enterprise organizations.

claims.claim: Turning tenant auditing off makes audit searches return no results.
claims.quote: When you turn off auditing, searches of the audit log in Microsoft Purview return no results. Running the Search-UnifiedAuditLog cmdlet in Exchange Online PowerShell also returns no results.

claims.claim: Get-AdminAuditLogConfig | Format-List UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled in Exchange Online PowerShell verifies the tenant audit setting.
claims.quote: To verify that auditing is turned on for your organization, run the following command in Exchange Online PowerShell: Get-AdminAuditLogConfig | Format-List UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope: Roles; Governance controls
claims.claim: Searching the audit log in the Purview portal requires Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Microsoft Purview portal to search the audit log.

claims.claim: Access to audit cmdlets requires Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs in the Exchange admin center.
claims.quote: To access audit cmdlets, you must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Exchange admin center.

claims.claim: A restricted administrator can search and export user-generated audit logs only within assigned administrative units.
claims.quote: A restricted admin can only search and export user-generated audit logs within the scope of their assigned administrative units.

claims.claim: An unrestricted administrator can access all audit logs, including non-user and system-account logs.
claims.quote: An unrestricted admin has access to all audit logs, including logs generated by non-user and system accounts.

Read audit-search, purview-permissions and purview-admin-units search excerpts; general scoping is documented, but the new records' user/non-user classification is not.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: An Entra role takes precedence at runtime over an overlapping scoped Purview role-group assignment.
claims.quote: If you assign both an Entra role and a scoped Microsoft Purview role group assignment to a user or group ... the Entra role takes precedence at runtime.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: For overlapping capabilities, the Entra role leaves effective access unscoped despite the scoped Purview assignment.
claims.quote: When both scoped Microsoft Purview role assignments and Entra roles are present, Entra roles always take precedence, and scoping applied through Administrative Units doesn't restrict the user's effective permissions for overlapping capabilities.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes permission checks and audit visibility, not an automated action.
claims.quote: Improving permission checks when users access the Microsoft Purview portal. Enhanced audit logs will provide clearer visibility into role and scoped-role access decisions, helping administrators troubleshoot access issues and monitor authorization outcomes.
